disease_label_per_paper: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome after loxapine dose increase with dantrolene and bromocriptine response
presentation_summary: 81-year-old man with schizoaffective disorder received loxapine and methotrimeprazine during hospitalization.
After methotrimeprazine was stopped and loxapine increased, he developed diaphoresis, tremulousness, urinary incontinence, cognitive impairment, fever, tachycardia, rigidity, and unsteady gait.
Initial temperature was 38.3 C, heart rate 128/min, WBC 11.7 x10^9/L, AST 82 U/L, and CK 1145 U/L.
CK increased to 2574 U/L and temperature rose to 39.3 C; urine myoglobin became positive while septic workup was normal.
Loxapine was stopped and he improved after dantrolene followed by bromocriptine.

risk_context.source_text_value: Loxapine and methotrimeprazine exposure occurred during admission.
Loxapine was increased after methotrimeprazine was stopped.

observations.source_text_value: Loxapine dose was increased before symptoms.
Rigidity and other parkinsonian features were present.
Urinary incontinence occurred during the episode.
Urine myoglobin test later became positive.

course_observations.source_text_value: CK rose to 2574 U/L the next afternoon.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Treating clinicians made a firm NMS diagnosis.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The report states a firm diagnosis of NMS was made.
The report describes a normal septic workup.

confirmatory_findings.finding: ECG showed no acute ischemic changes, and CK-MB/troponin were normal.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: Cardiac ischemia markers did not support myocardial infarction.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Symptoms and CK improved after stopping loxapine and giving dantrolene then bromocriptine.
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: The report describes clinical improvement after these interventions.

quality_warnings: The final diagnosis, normal septic workup, cardiac exclusion, and treatment response are preserved but excluded from ordinary ranking.
Ordinary ranking evidence emphasizes dopamine antagonist exposure, recent dose change, fever, rigidity/parkinsonism, autonomic features, CK rise, urine myoglobin, leukocytosis, and AST elevation.
